_meta.source: In-game Notice 'Update Log' for the Airship Trade update, four screenshots captured by XYIAN (Kyle) on 2026-10-15, transcribed verbatim at docs/game-knowledge/updates/2026-10-15-airship-trade.md together with one statement he made in the same session. Three screens are the Update Log at different scroll positions; the fourth is a popup whose banner reads 'New Feature Unlocked' over the text 'Personal Trade unlocked!' on his own account. The Notice carousel alternates a 'Hotfix' banner and the older 'Version 1.1.9' banner over one continuous log; the log prints NO version number for this update, so nothing here calls it a version or Version 1.1.9. 'Hotfix' is the only label the game gives it.
_meta.confidence: High for everything printed in the notice — every quoted string is byte-identical to the transcript, which was verified line by line against the four images. Dates: the notice's own '*Airship Trade opens on October 19 (UTC)' (recorded as 19 October 2026, UTC) and the 15 October 2026 capture date; the notice prints no publication date, so entries say 'captured 15 October 2026', never 'announced on'. Entries are worded to stay true after the mode opens rather than asserting it is unopened. The one thing observed live is the 'Personal Trade unlocked!' popup on XYIAN's account on 15 October 2026, four days before the opening date, recorded as his account's state with no unlock requirement invented. The notice names a great deal it never explains — cargo, cargo quality, cabin slots, the Central Trading Post, the trade map, guards, bounties, trade resources, transport rewards, the defense lineup — and those are listed as not documented; per the v3.36.3 lesson that a directive beside data gets recited instead of the data, only ONE entry (what_is_not_documented) carries the !suggest instruction and the five part entries end in a neutral 'Not documented:' list. Nothing is inferred from the names: Guild Trade is not called a Guild hub building, Trade Raids are not filed under Arena, and no entry point is claimed — the Home screens in these captures are partly covered by popups, so they cannot show that no button exists. Homonym guards, all grounded in entries this knowledge base already holds: Trade Raids against Guild Raid, Monster Invasion and Quick Raid (guarded from BOTH sides — guild.guild_raid.relation_to_monster_invasion is repaired to name all four); the Airship Trade defense lineup against the Arena defending loadout; Twinborn dismantling against rune salvage; the Griffin Amulet cap against the Guild Expedition DMG Reflect talent; and the word 'trade' against the Guild Merchant bargain and the event shops. The naming alias comes only from the guild owner's own words on 15 October 2026 and is attributed to him; it deliberately does NOT teach that the bare word 'trade' means this mode. 'Guild Expedition S5' is recorded as printed, with which season S5 is left undocumented. Guild Trade's reward list names 'Characters', so the two hero-shard source enumerations include it inside the enumeration, with shards-vs-heroes stated as unknown; the parallel primacy claims about shard, gear and rune sources are caveated where the new source could falsify them (event_shop.advice.legendary_shard_path) and left alone where the notice gives no rarity or category to falsify them (gear_sets.s_ranked_source, runes.how_to_get_etched_runes), which is stated here deliberately rather than left as an asymmetry. Gameplay Improvement 2 ('Improved chat history loading') gets its own entry so every one of the five improvements is retrievable. The Griffin Amulet cap is quoted in the notice's own form, 'ATK*10000', so a member quoting it retrieves the entry, and it gets its own key rather than living only at the end of a 600-character stat list.

airship_trade.overview: Airship Trade is a new game mode introduced by the in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026 as 'New Mode: Airship Trade' and summed up there as 'Set sail with Guild members, escort cargo, and fight for resources across the trade world!'. It opens on 19 October 2026 (printed '*Airship Trade opens on October 19 (UTC)'); on the 15 October 2026 capture date it had been announced and had not opened yet, so if today is on or after 19 October 2026 it should be live. It has five named parts, each with its own entry here: (1) Guild Trade, (2) Personal Trade, (3) Trade Raids, (4) Escort & Wanted, (5) Trade World. 'Personal Trade' names part 2 only; the whole mode is Airship Trade. The guild owner XYIAN, introducing the mode on 15 October 2026, reached for several names for it — 'personal trade / trade / airship or airshop trade' — so a member may use any of those; no source here records settled member usage, and 'airshop' is one letter from 'airship'. The word 'trade' is also used in this knowledge base for the Guild Merchant bargain mechanic and for event shops that exchange participation for stock, and neither of those is Airship Trade. On 15 October 2026 XYIAN's own account showed a popup whose banner read 'New Feature Unlocked' over the text 'Personal Trade unlocked!', four days before the stated opening date; the notice does not explain that, and nothing records what unlocks the feature or whether the rest of the mode opened early for anyone.
airship_trade.guild_trade: Guild Trade is part 1 of Airship Trade (in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026), printed in full as: 'Work with Guild members, compete for cabin slots, and escort cargo to the Central Trading Post to earn Gear, Characters, Runes, Mystlings, and more!'. So the rewards named are Gear, Characters, Runes and Mystlings, and the notice adds 'and more' without naming anything else. It gives no rarity, set or rune category for any of them, so it does not change what the gear and rune source entries elsewhere say. Not documented: what a cabin slot is, how members compete for one, what cargo is, where the Central Trading Post sits, how an escort is run and what it costs; whether 'Characters' means hero shards or whole heroes, and which heroes (see characters.shards); and whether the Mystlings arrive as eggs or as hatched creatures.
airship_trade.personal_trade: Personal Trade is part 2 of Airship Trade (in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026), printed in full as: 'Send out your Personal Airship and refresh cargo quality freely. Higher quality means better transport rewards!'. So the mode gives you a Personal Airship once Personal Trade is unlocked (XYIAN's own account showed a 'Personal Trade unlocked!' popup on 15 October 2026 — what unlocks it is not stated), cargo carried on it has a quality, that quality can be refreshed 'freely', and higher quality gives better transport rewards. A Personal Airship can be raided by other players (see trade_raids and escort_and_wanted). 'Personal Trade' is the name of this part; the mode as a whole is Airship Trade. Not documented: what the quality tiers are, what 'freely' costs or limits, how long a run takes, and what the transport rewards are.
airship_trade.trade_raids: Trade Raids is part 3 of Airship Trade (in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026), printed in full as: 'Find other players' Guild or Personal Airships on the trade map and start PVP battles. Defeat the guards to loot their cargo!'. So a Trade Raid is a PvP battle against another player's Guild Airship or Personal Airship, found on the trade map, in which you defeat guards to loot cargo. In this game four different features use the word raid and none of them is the others: Trade Raids (this one, player-versus-player airship raids), Guild Raid (a guild mode), Monster Invasion (a guild boss battle, also called MI) and the Quick Raid button that auto-resolves a cleared stage. A question about raiding another PLAYER is Trade Raids. If a member says only 'raid' and nothing in the question says which feature is meant, ask which one; if they name Monster Invasion, MI, Guild Raid or Quick Raid, answer from that feature's own entry. Not documented: what the guards are, how a raid is entered, how often one may be run, and what the player raided loses.
airship_trade.escort_and_wanted: Escort & Wanted is part 4 of Airship Trade (in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026), printed in full as: 'Set a defense lineup to protect your cargo! If your Personal Airship is raided, place a bounty on the opponent and strike back!'. So you set a defense lineup to protect cargo, and being raided lets you place a bounty on the raider and strike back. This defense lineup is part of Airship Trade and is not stated to be the same thing as the defending loadout in the standard Arena. Not documented: what a defense lineup consists of, what a bounty costs or grants, and whether striking back is itself a Trade Raid.
airship_trade.trade_world: Trade World is part 5 of Airship Trade (in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026), printed in full as: 'Explore the new trade map, view Airship routes in real time, share raid targets with other players, and compete for trade resources!'. So there is a trade map that can be explored, Airship routes are visible in real time, raid targets can be shared with other players, and players compete for trade resources. Not documented: what a trade resource is, who raid targets can be shared with, and how the map is navigated.
airship_trade.trading_items_with_another_player: No general item trading between players is documented. Everything the Airship Trade notice (in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026) says about the mode is escorting your own cargo, raiding other players' airships and competing for resources; it does not mention giving, swapping, selling or mailing an item, a hero, a rune or a currency to another specific player. Across this whole knowledge base the one documented player-to-player gift is the 3-Day Friend Trial Cards that come with the Privilege Card Deal Pack. If a member asks whether they can trade an item to a friend or guildmate, say that no general item trading is documented, that Airship Trade is a cargo-escort and raid mode rather than a described item-swap system, and point at !suggest. The Guild Merchant bargain mechanic and the event shops exchange currency for stock rather than items between players, so they do not answer this question.
airship_trade.what_is_not_documented: Named in the Airship Trade notice (in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026) and nowhere explained: cargo and cargo quality, cabin slots, the Central Trading Post, the trade map and trade world, Airship routes, guards, bounties, trade resources, transport rewards, and the defense lineup. Also not documented: where Airship Trade is entered from (no entry point was captured and the notice names none), whether it appears under the Events tab or among the Guild hub buildings, what unlocks it, whether it costs energy or any other currency, whether it runs in seasons, and whether it has its own shop or currency. Say so and point at !suggest rather than guessing from the names.

game_modes.overview: There are four main game-mode categories: Campaign, Arena, Challenge, and Dungeon. Each contains sub-modes with different mechanics and rewards. Airship Trade, introduced by the in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026 and opening 19 October 2026, is a further mode; the notice calls it a 'New Mode' and does not say whether it joins those four categories, sits under the Events tab or stands on its own (see airship_trade.overview).

arena.overview: Arena is the PvP category. Sub-modes: Main Arena, Peak Arena, Rumble Ladder, All-Star Cup, and Mega All-Star Cup. Trade Raids, part of the Airship Trade mode introduced by the in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026, are also PvP battles, but the notice does not place them under Arena and they are not an Arena sub-mode (see airship_trade.trade_raids).

game_modes.events_tab: The Events tab groups three categories: Arena (Main Arena, Peak Arena, Rumble Ladder, All-Star Cup and Mega All-Star Cup — see arena.overview), Challenge (Magic Plant Defense, Seal Battle, Sky Tower) and Dungeon (Abyssal Tide, Gold Cave, Shackled Jungle). Each sub-feature has its own season or cycle, rewards and shop. Those three categories are what was captured before 15 October 2026; whether the Airship Trade mode introduced by the notice captured that day (opening 19 October 2026) appears under this tab is not documented — see game_modes.airship_trade.

dungeon.shackled_jungle_stage_ranges: Shackled Jungle stages are numbered in one continuous sequence. Update 1.1.7 added stages 1501-1700 (the 1.1.7 note called them 'chapters' — same thing), and Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026) added stages 1701-2150, so 2150 is the highest Shackled Jungle stage recorded here as of 17 September 2026. Earlier ranges are not recorded. Separately, the in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026 reduced the difficulty of Shackled Jungle Stage 1600 — the notice names Stage 1600 and no other stage, within the 1501-1700 range; it adds no new stages and does not change the highest stage, which is still 2150.

challenge.magic_plant_defense_rewards: Clear rewards include Mystling Eggs and Mystling materials, which makes it the primary documented source for hatching new Mystlings. Drops vary by stage and higher stages drop better. In co-op the host's drop rates apply and assisting players get reduced rates. Recorded before 15 October 2026: the Airship Trade notice of that date names Mystlings among the Guild Trade rewards without saying whether they arrive as eggs or as hatched creatures, so whether Magic Plant Defense is still the largest source is not documented (see game_modes.airship_trade.guild_trade).

main_screen.hub_entry_points: The main screen (the Home screen) is the hub for everything else: Hunt (a quick-reward alternative to farming stages), Reach (current campaign progress such as 123-50, which opens the clearance rewards), Guild, Camp (Mystlings), Rankings, Task Center, Friends, a Rumble Ladder mode shortcut (added in Version 1.1.9, in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026; its position on the screen is not stated), and the five bottom tabs Shop, Gear, Campaign, Collectible and Events. Where Airship Trade (in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026, opening 19 October 2026) is reached from is not documented: the notice names no entry point, and no screen showing one was captured — the Home screen in those captures is partly covered by popups, so nothing there settles whether a button exists.
main_screen.chat_history_loading: The in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026 lists, under Gameplay Improvements, 'Improved chat history loading.' That is the whole statement: which chat (guild, world or private), what was wrong and what changed are not described — say so and point at !suggest.

guild.hub_buildings: Guild Hall (members, roles, research, leaderboard), Monster Invasion (the daily guild boss battle, MI), Guild Expedition (multi-guild PvP tournament), Shop / Guild Store (hero shards and random Epic runes), Guild Merchant (community bargain mechanic), and Guild Aid. The Starlight Gala was added later and is not in this list. Guild Raid (see guild_raid) is also not in this list; whether it is the same feature as Monster Invasion is not documented. Guild Trade, part of the Airship Trade mode introduced by the in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026, involves working with Guild members, but the notice does not say it is a Guild hub building or where it is entered from — see game_modes.airship_trade.guild_trade.

guild_raid.relation_to_monster_invasion: Whether Guild Raid is the same feature as Monster Invasion (the daily guild boss battle, MI, documented under monster_invasion) or a separate mode is not documented. Do not answer a Guild Raid question with Monster Invasion details, or the reverse; say the relationship is not documented and point at !suggest. If the member says Monster Invasion or MI, answer from monster_invasion. Four different features in this game use the word raid and none of them is the others: Guild Raid (this entry), Monster Invasion (a guild boss battle), the Quick Raid button that auto-resolves a cleared stage or attempt, and — from the in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026 — Trade Raids, the player-versus-player airship raids in the Airship Trade mode (see game_modes.airship_trade.trade_raids). A question about raiding another PLAYER is Trade Raids, not Guild Raid.

guild_expedition.guild_expedition_s5_avatar_frame: The in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026 lists, under Gameplay Improvements, 'Improved the avatar frame for Guild Expedition S5'. That is the whole statement: what changed about the frame is not described. 'S5' is how the notice prints it; no source here numbers the Guild Expedition seasons, so which season S5 is is not documented. This knowledge base records a Guild Expedition season opening 5 October 2026 that adds the Starbound Eternity tier (see starbound_eternity_season_october_2026), but the notice does not say whether S5 is that season. Do not state that S5 is the Starbound Eternity season; say the link is not documented and point at !suggest.

griffin_amulet.quality_skills: ATK PWR +17,160, ATK PWR +5%, CRIT DMG +12%, Counter with 2x / 4x DMG to nearby enemies when damaged, ATK PWR +10%, Amulet's base stats +20% / +30% / +40%, When taking DMG within distance of 7, chance to drop Hearts (The counterattack and reflect behaviour above was recorded before 15 October 2026 — see counterattack_cap_october_2026.)
griffin_amulet.counterattack_cap_october_2026: The in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026 changed the Griffin Amulet under Gameplay Improvements, printing: 'Fixed an issue where Griffin Amulet reflect damage could trigger twice; Griffin Amulet counterattack damage is now capped at player ATK*10000 per hit.' The cap is printed exactly as 'ATK*10000', meaning 10,000 times the player's ATK. The notice does not say whether its 'reflect damage' and its 'counterattack damage' are the same effect, nor which of the quality-skill lines they refer to, and it does not use the word nerf — but a double-trigger fix and a damage cap are both reductions to how much the counterattack can do. Do not confuse either with the Guild Expedition DMG Reflect talent, which is a different thing. Everything else about the Griffin Amulet is unchanged — see quality_skills.

weapons.pve_vs_pvp_rankings: Gear set rankings differ drastically between PvE and PvP. For PvE/campaign: Oracle is best, then Dragoon, then Griffin. For PvP: Griffin is best, then Dragoon, then Oracle. Dragoon is the best of both worlds and the perfect happy medium — if you want to optimize for one mode, lean Oracle (PvE) or Griffin (PvP). This ranking was recorded before Version 1.1.9 (in-game Notice captured 17 September 2026), which rebalanced the Dragoon Set with new affixes and added an old/new version switch for it; whether the ranking still holds after that change is not documented. This ranking also predates the in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026, which capped Griffin Amulet counterattack damage at player ATK*10000 per hit and fixed its reflect damage triggering twice; whether Griffin is still first for PvP after that change is not documented.

twinborn_runes.dismantling: Equipped or preset Twinborn Runes can be dismantled: the in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026 lifted that restriction under Gameplay Improvements, printing 'Equipped or preset Twinborn Runes can now be dismantled, making Rune adjustments easier. Locked Runes must still be unlocked first.' So a Twinborn rune no longer has to be unequipped or removed from a preset first, and a locked rune must still be unlocked before it can be dismantled. Whether unequipped Twinborn runes could already be dismantled before that is not stated. Not documented: what dismantling returns — whether the two merged runes come back, and whether any of the Twinborn Cores or scraps spent on the merge are refunded — where the dismantle button lives, and what it costs. The notice does not say whether dismantling a Twinborn rune is the same operation as salvaging an ordinary rune for scraps (see cost_in_twinborn_cores) — do not assume it is.

characters.shards: Heroes are unlocked and starred up with shards, shown as an 'X/Y' counter on the hero card (X/50, X/100 and X/150 counters observed — see star_system.how_stars_are_earned for where each was seen). Sources: Daily Rewards Bonus Pack, Limited Offer packs, events, and — per the in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026 — Guild Trade, which lists 'Characters' among the rewards for escorting cargo to the Central Trading Post; the notice does not say whether 'Characters' means hero shards or whole heroes, or which heroes, so treat it as an undocumented hero source (see game_modes.airship_trade.guild_trade). Not Hunt.

hero_shards.sources: Daily Rewards (Bonus Pack), Limited Offer packs, events, and — per the in-game Notice captured 15 October 2026 — Guild Trade, which names 'Characters' among its rewards without saying whether those are shards or whole heroes (see characters.shards). Not Hunt — Hunt does not drop hero shards (see hunt.reward_types).

advice.legendary_shard_path: Island Treasure Hunt events trade event participation (Island Points) for Legendary hero shards - Otta, Thor, Cleo - that the standard Guild Store does not stock, since it only carries Rare. Events are the primary Legendary hero progression path for active F2P players. Recorded before 15 October 2026, when the Airship Trade notice named 'Characters' among the Guild Trade rewards without saying which heroes or whether they are shards; whether events are still the primary Legendary path is not documented (see characters.shards).

custom_facts.text: The in-game Notice 'Update Log' captured 15 October 2026 introduced a new mode, Airship Trade, opening 19 October 2026 (UTC). The notice prints no version number — do not call this update Version 1.1.9 or give it any version number; the carousel shows the older Version 1.1.9 banner (that 17 September 2026 notice is a different update) beside a new banner captioned 'Hotfix', which is the only label the game gives this one. This 15 October 2026 notice is the most recent update recorded in this knowledge base; Version 1.1.9 (17 September 2026) is the one before it. Airship Trade has five parts: Guild Trade (work with guild members, compete for cabin slots, escort cargo to the Central Trading Post for Gear, Characters, Runes and Mystlings), Personal Trade (send out your Personal Airship and refresh cargo quality; higher quality means better transport rewards), Trade Raids (find other players' Guild or Personal Airships on the trade map and start PvP battles, defeating the guards to loot their cargo), Escort & Wanted (set a defense lineup to protect cargo, and place a bounty on whoever raids your Personal Airship), and Trade World (explore the trade map, view Airship routes in real time, share raid targets, and compete for trade resources). The same notice listed five Gameplay Improvements: equipped or preset Twinborn Runes can now be dismantled, though locked runes must be unlocked first; chat history loading was improved; the Guild Expedition S5 avatar frame was improved; the difficulty of Shackled Jungle Stage 1600 was reduced; and a Griffin Amulet fix stopped reflect damage triggering twice and capped Griffin Amulet counterattack damage at player ATK*10000 per hit. The per-item entries hold the detail; much of what the notice names it never explains.
